essence: Shift Channels rebuilds the output RGBA channels independently by choosing which source channel feeds each destination channel. Changing a Take Red/Green/Blue selector reroutes that output color component; changing Take Alpha From reroutes transparency, so a color channel can become a matte or the existing alpha can be preserved.
when_to_use: convert a channel into a matte
manifests_as: The image's colors, color separation, and/or transparency change according to which original channel is copied into each output channel.

key_levers.name: Take Alpha From
key_levers.effect: Selects the source used for output transparency; preserving the default keeps the original alpha, while selecting a color-derived source makes transparency follow that source.

key_levers.name: Take Red From
key_levers.effect: Selects which source supplies the output red component; choosing another color channel swaps or duplicates that channel into red.

key_levers.name: Take Green From
key_levers.effect: Selects which source supplies the output green component; matching all RGB outputs to one source produces a monochrome rendition of that source channel.

key_levers.name: Take Blue From
key_levers.effect: Selects which source supplies the output blue component; changing it is especially useful for blue/red swaps and channel-isolation looks.

key_levers.name: Effect Opacity
key_levers.effect: Mixes the effect's channel-remapped result with the unmodified layer; lower values reduce the visible strength of the remap.

config_recipes.Identity / no visible change: Take Alpha From 1, Take Red From 2, Take Green From 3, Take Blue From 4, Effect Opacity 100%.
config_recipes.Red-blue swap: Take Alpha From 1, Take Red From 4, Take Green From 3, Take Blue From 2, Effect Opacity 100%.
config_recipes.Green-channel monochrome: Take Alpha From 1, Take Red From 3, Take Green From 3, Take Blue From 3, Effect Opacity 100%.
config_recipes.Red-channel monochrome: Take Alpha From 1, Take Red From 2, Take Green From 2, Take Blue From 2, Effect Opacity 100%.

reasoning_hooks: The defaults are an identity mapping, so adding the effect produces no visible change until at least one Take selector differs from its default.
Each destination is independent: selecting the same source for Red, Green, and Blue duplicates that source into grayscale-like RGB, rather than isolating it as a colored channel.

Alpha is causally separate from RGB. A dramatic color remap can leave the silhouette unchanged if Take Alpha From remains at its default; conversely, changing alpha can hide or reveal pixels without changing their RGB values.
Use Effect Opacity only after establishing the desired channel routing: it blends the remapped result back toward the original rather than choosing channel sources.
